{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/trial.csv')

# Count total rows and unique patient_id
n_rows = len(df)
n_unique_patients = df['patient_id'].nunique()

# Count how many duplicate patient_id entries exist (i.e., how many times a patient appears more than once)
duplicate_count = n_rows - n_unique_patients

# Confirm this is exactly 48, and that it corresponds to 24 re-tested patients
n_retested_patients = duplicate_count // 2

# Deduplicate by keeping the row with the highest sample_seq per patient
df_dedup = df.loc[df.groupby('patient_id')['sample_seq'].idxmax()]

# Final number of unique patients after deduplication
num_patients = len(df_dedup)

# Print all required numbers
print(f"Total rows: {n_rows}")
print(f"Unique patient_id: {n_unique_patients}")
print(f"Number of duplicate patient_id entries: {duplicate_count}")
print(f"Number of re-tested patients (each appears twice): {n_retested_patients}")
print(f"Number of patients after deduplication (keeping max sample_seq per patient): {num_patients}")

# Verify that the deduplicated set has no duplicates
assert df_dedup['patient_id'].duplicated().sum() == 0, "Deduplicated dataset still has duplicates"

# Final check: does the deduplicated count match the unique count?
assert num_patients == n_unique_patients, f"Deduplicated count {num_patients} does not match unique count {n_unique_patients}""}
